native-shim.role: control: the 11 shimmed sources (int64.sh) compiled natively, measures what the Int64 shim costs on a 64-bit target (nothing on 9 of the 11); defined for the 11 shimmed benchmarks only

versions.swift: 6.2.0 (swift-6.2-RELEASE, image swift:6.2.0), same compiler for native and wasm; the matrix pins swift:6.1 (6.1.3)
versions.wasmSdk: swift-6.2-RELEASE_wasm.artifactbundle.tar.gz sha256 fe4e8648309fce86ea522e9e0d1dc48e82df6ba6e5743dbf0c53db8429fb5224 (swift.org release 6.2, Wasm SDK; no wasm SDK exists for 6.1.x)
versions.nativeFlags: swiftc -O (the matrix build line, dynamic stdlib)
versions.wasmFlags: swiftc -O -target wasm32-unknown-wasip1 -sdk WASI.sdk -resource-dir swift_static -static-stdlib -Xclang-linker -resource-dir -Xclang-linker swift_static/clang -Xlinker -z -Xlinker stack-size=8388608

transforms: int64.sh (languages/wasm/swift/int64.sh + int64-shim.swift), wasm build of 11 benchmarks only (dijkstra gbdt gemm k-means lz77 polymorphism reverse-complement sha256 sort-search viterbi vm): inserts after `import Foundation` typealiases making untyped integer literals, Int and UInt 64-bit, plus Array Int64 subscript/init/reserveCapacity overloads. Needed because Swift's Int is 32 bits on wasm32. Measured natively by the native-shim column: identical on 9 of the 11, dijkstra +0.88%, sha256 +0.098%. The other 7 benchmarks are built from the unmodified canonical source.
asymmetries: Swift version: the matrix is 6.1.3 but the first official wasm SDK is 6.2; native and wasm both use 6.2.0 here, so the native column is not the matrix Swift cell
wasm links the stdlib and Foundation statically (-static-stdlib, from the SDK toolset); native links them dynamically, as in the matrix. Startup cancels in the differential

wasm32 Int is 32 bits: the 11 shimmed benchmarks run with Int64 (emulating the native 64-bit Int); array indexing then truncates an Int64 to the 32-bit address index, an extra wrap that native does not have. The other 7 run with the real 32-bit Int on wasm and 64-bit Int natively
wasm shadow stack raised to 8 MiB (SDK default 64 KiB) to match the native 8 MiB main-thread stack
wasm32-wasip1 libc is wasi-libc (dlmalloc) with Swift's wasm runtime; native uses glibc malloc
no -swift-sdk option in swiftc 6.2: the SDK is wired by hand with -sdk/-resource-dir/-static-stdlib exactly as its swift-sdk.json and toolset.json specify
the native column is aarch64 machine code, so ratios mix ISA with wasm cost; native is run under the gcc:14/trixie base (not the matrix swift image) with swift runtime libs copied to /opt/swift-rt
the Int64 shim is not a perfect no-op natively: the native-shim column matches the unmodified native build exactly on 9 of the 11 shimmed benchmarks, dijkstra is +0.88% and sha256 +0.098%

cellMarks.note: Swift: wasm built with the Int64 shim (int64.sh); the unmarked Swift cells run the unmodified source with wasm32's native 32-bit Int

compileError.vm: integer literal '4294967295' overflows when stored into 'Int'

unchangedSourcesOnWasm32.trapOrWrong: the other 10 trap on `unreachable` (overflow or bounds) or print a wrong checksum (dijkstra prints 0)

checkedMultiply.finding: Swift's overflow-checked 64-bit multiply lowers on wasm32 to a call to __multi3 (a straight-line helper of about 130 wasm instructions; aarch64 uses mul + smulh/umulh) followed by a high-word overflow test. The hot loop of bigint, gemm, k-means and viterbi calls it (once per innermost iteration in bigint and gemm, about 1.3 per innermost iteration in k-means, about 73 per timestep in viterbi).
checkedMultiply.how: diagnostic only, outside the benchmark sources: scratch copies with wrapping &* on the hot multiplies (k-means and viterbi also wrap the adjacent index additions), built with the same swiftc 6.2.0 flags and the int64 shim; checksums identical; qemu insn differentials, wasmtime 50
checkedMultiply.instructionsPerCall: about 131 to 138 (bigint exact: 5,550,104 calls in the differential, 727.1M instructions)
checkedMultiply.shimRole: in gemm, k-means and viterbi the 64-bit multiplies come from the Int64 shim (native Int is 64-bit, so the work matches native); unshimmed 32-bit builds have no __multi3 call but are wrong on wasm32. bigint uses UInt64 explicitly and is unshimmed

v8Seed.finding: Swift seeds its Hasher (Dictionary, Set) from WASI random_get; making run-node.mjs return a fixed byte stream moved k-nucleotide's V8 differential by -0.195% and no other V8 cell by more than 0.05%
v8Seed.measured: 2026-10-29 V8 column vs 2026-10-27, qemu insn differentials
